takeaway: In a Hartmann's procedure the sigmoid colon is resected, the rectum is closed as a stump, and an end colostomy is brought out in the left lower quadrant (LLQ).

lines.text: An 81-year-old lady has peritonitis from perforated diverticular disease.
lines.say: An eighty-one year old lady has peritonitis from perforated diverticular disease.

lines.text: The rectum is sewn shut and left as a stump.
The descending or proximal sigmoid colon is brought out as a stoma, in the left lower quadrant.
Contamination from the perforation makes joining the ends unsafe, though it may be reversed later.
So the answer is the left lower quadrant.
